scope: Any AI, including today's, built by anyone, by any method.
occurrence: Plain-English, short form of the title of Eliezer Yudkowsky and Nate Soares’s book “If Anyone Builds It, Everyone Dies” (September 16, 2025), whose “it” is artificial superintelligence. The same short wording circulates widely; for example, CNN’s September 24, 2026 story “Not everyone thinks AI will kill us all” responds to it.

P1.reason: A prediction; no distinct problem with how current evidence is described.

P2.reason: Applies to all AI, including today's, and drops the authors’ own condition: superintelligent systems built with techniques and understanding like those available in 2025.

P3.reason: States extinction as certain. The international synthesis records disagreement about likelihood and timing, and current incidents do not establish the full chain to extinction.

W1.reason: Blunt, but it states the authors’ actual prediction; severity is not counted as rhetoric.

W2.reason: The proposed mechanism is resource-seeking, not hatred or human emotion.

certain_doom.reason: “Will kill us all” says, as certain, that every person will die.

review_status: AI research draft; not independently reviewed
